text:
maya: Heads-up — I'm about to open a PR for a small refactor I'm calling 'duty-cycle prefetch'. The idea is to split ownership between the local prefetcher (fast path) and global admission (memory quotas) to reduce churn on hot prefixes. I'm worried about a corner where demote+evict races could produce stale reads. looking for quick thoughts.

jon: can you sketch the flow in 2 lines?

maya: high-level: local prefetch serves hot requests and keeps short-lived residency; global admission controls long-term residency and reclaims memory. on handoff we transfer an ownership ticket.

maya: config snippet:
```
prefetch:
  duty_cycle_ms: 250
  ownership_split_percent: 30
```

sophia: concern: if global admission decides to reclaim before local drain finishes, we could evict while there are inflight readers. that'd make reads after demote see stale state.

sam: one mitigation is an epoch pin on handoff. handoff increments epoch; readers read epoch on start and verify it at commit. eviction only proceeds when epoch stable or timeout.

alex: we tried epoch pin vibes before — it added an extra check for long-lived cursors and spiked p99 a bit. can we avoid blocking the hot path?

jon: alternative: soft-evict state. mark prefix as demoting, let inflight readers gracefully finish (track inflight count), prevent immediate memory reclaim until inflight==0 or we hit an evict_timeout. global admission can still stop new prefetch placements but not reclaim physical memory.

maya: that sounds cleaner. what metrics do we need to be confident?

sophia: at minimum: inflight_reads_per_prefix, demote_marked_ts, evict_timeout_count, stale_read_rate (read-after-write mismatches). also histogram for time_between_demote_and_reclaim.

sam: add a canary plan: 1% of nodes run the split model, sample prefixes and compare read-after-write traces against baseline. fail-fast if stale_read_rate > 0.01% for sampled traffic.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout queued at 1%. dashboard: https://deploys/release/8743219999

maya: plan I'll put in the PR: 1) feature flag behind config 2) implement soft-evict + epoch fallback 3) add metrics and perf test 4) 1% canary, then 10%, then full roll if no regressions.

alex: if we see latency regression on streaming cursors, fallback: disable epoch pin for cursors labeled `long-lived` (preserve old behavior), and document tradeoffs.

sophia: we need a regression harness: demote while a streaming cursor reads then writes, assert no stale read observed. ideally simulate network jitter and prefetch delays.

sam: I can sketch the harness and a small chaos scenario today. will add steps to the PR checklist.

maya: thanks. i'll open the PR with the design rationale + QA checklist and tag eng-sre for observability verification.

jon: small naming nit: 'duty-cycle' feels ephemeral. maybe call the feature `split-prefetch-admission` in code, and keep 'duty-cycle' as the experiment name?

maya: good call — will rename in the PR. thx everyone :raised_hands:

jon: :thumbsup:

maya: leaving this open for another hour in case anyone wants to add perf numbers. otherwise i'll land the feature-flagged draft PR later today.
